description: A curated catalogue of awesome agentic AI patterns

summary.one_liner: A curated, pattern-first catalogue of real-world agentic AI patterns (workflows, tricks, and mini-architectures) for autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents used in production.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is an "awesome" style list of agentic AI patterns, each backed by a public reference such as a blog post, talk, repo, or paper. Patterns must be repeatable (used by more than one team), agent-centric (improving how an agent senses, reasons, or acts), and traceable to a source. The README groups the patterns into eight categories: Context & Memory, Feedback Loops, Learning & Adaptation, Orchestration & Control, Reliability & Eval, Security & Safety, Tool Use & Environment, and UX & Collaboration. Each category lists pattern titles as links, and the tables are auto-generated from a patterns/ folder. The README also points to a companion website (source in apps/web/) with a pattern explorer, compare tool, decision guide, and graph view, plus an llms.txt file for AI assistants.
use_cases: Finding a named pattern for a specific agent problem, such as context compaction or sub-agent spawning
Comparing approaches to multi-agent orchestration and coordination
Browsing security and safety patterns for coding or tool-using agents
Looking up feedback loop and evaluation techniques for agent reliability
Learning how production teams handle agent memory and context windows
Contributing a new agent pattern to a shared catalogue
how_to_run: Browse the category sections in the README or visit the companion website
To contribute: fork the repo and create a branch (git checkout -b add-my-pattern)
Add a pattern file under patterns/ using the template
Run bun run build:data to refresh the generated README sections and site data
notable: Patterns must be used by more than one team and backed by a public reference
Organized into eight categories covering the full agent lifecycle
Companion website with pattern explorer, compare tool, decision explorer, and graph visualization
Ships an llms.txt file so AI assistants can recommend patterns
README tables are generated from the patterns/ folder
caveats: Pattern-first curation: product announcements and promotions are rejected
Categories are described as fluid and may change
